title: Water cycle diagram sheet
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y7 lesson 14 (Water cycle diagram sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 14: Meet the River Thames: the water cycle at work. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: The River Thames
points: Flows east through Oxford and London to the North Sea

model.title: Why does the Thames keep flowing in a dry summer?

parts.text: Rain from earlier months soaked into rock
Groundwater seeps slowly into the river
So the river is fed even without rain

keywords.def: the constant movement of water between sea, air and land
water falling as rain, snow or hail

questions.q: Describe the course of the Thames. (3 marks)
questions.a: Rises near Kemble in Gloucestershire (1), flows east through Oxford and London (1), into the North Sea via its estuary (1)

questions.q: Which stage happens when the Sun heats the sea?
Core: Draw and label a water cycle diagram with six terms, then add arrows showing three routes water takes to reach the Thames.
questions.a: Accurate diagram with evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, run-off, groundwater flow

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain how London's paved surfaces change the water cycle.
questions.a: Less infiltration, more fast run-off into drains and rivers

questions.q: Stretch: Why is the water cycle called a closed system?
questions.a: No water is added or lost overall; it just moves between stores

questions.q: Water vapour cooling into droplets is:
questions.a: B) Condensation. Condensation turns vapour back into liquid droplets in clouds.

questions.q: Big question: where does the Thames' water come from?
questions.a: Rain falling on its drainage basin, reaching it by run-off, through soil and as groundwater
